deities: Goddess Bhadrakali (Porkkali Bhagavathy) - main deity, fierce warlike aspect, wooden idol of Kadu Sharkara yogam in standing pose with 4 arms (lotus, sword, goblet, shield), facing west; an archana bimbam is used for rites since the moolavar is daru silpam
Lord Shiva (separate sanctum, silalingam, facing east)
Sapta Mathrukkal - Brahmani, Vaishnavi, Shankari, Kaumari, Varahi, Chamundi, Indrani (Mathrusaala shrine facing north)
festivals: Annual Pooram Festival - 9 days in Meenam (March-April), Karthika to Uthram nakshatra; opens with Kalarippayattu performance; Thayambaka, Poorakkali, fireworks on final day
Theyyam Kaliyattam - Kalarivathukkal Amma's Theyyam with the tallest Thirumudi (headgear) among Kannur theyyams

history.dynasty: Chirakkal royal family (scion of the Kolathiri/Mooshika kings)
history.period: Built around 10th century per one travel source (weakly sourced - verify); legend attributes consecration to Parasurama
history.summary: The temple is the family shrine of the erstwhile Chirakkal royal family, successors of the Kolathiri dynasty (descendants of the Mooshika kings), who relocated their capital from Ezhimala to Chirakkal near the Valapattanam river. It was originally worshipped by the Vadakke Illam and later forcefully handed over to / acquired by the Chirakkal Kovilakom, which renovated it with large attached properties. It is one of the Devi temple triad of the Chirakkal Kingdom - the others being Cherukunnu Annapoorneshwari and Tiruvarkadu (Madayi Kavu) Bhagavathy; mythology says the three goddesses arrived by boat from Kasi together. The name derives from 'Kalari Vaatilkal' - the temple is revered as the mother of the martial art Kalarippayattu, whose practitioners take the goddess as patron. The architecture follows Rurujith Vidhanam (Kaula Shakteya Sampradaya) with four sanctums. It is administered by the Malabar Devaswom Board as a Category A temple. CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Kannur town - it stands at Valapattanam, on the banks of the Valapattanam river, about 8 km from Kannur town. Documented with the corrected location.
